function: a procedural gear factory: slot x element-flavour x level -> equippable loot
label: armory
reuse: the world-generation lever pointed at GEAR (sibling of bestiary for creatures, affixes for rarity): forge_gear composes a base equippable from equip-slot x element-flavour x level (level-scaled mods, deduped prototype); arm_guardians gives every generated non-ambient guardian a themed gear drop and returns the prototypes to merge into ITEMS. The base is the floor; combat's affix factory rolls rarity + named affixes on top at defeat. Deterministic/pure.
notes: Merged into ITEMS in world.py after the wildlands merge, before inspect_world_links, so generated drop prototypes pass the same boot gate as authored gear. Ambient wildlife and already-dropping foes are left untouched. Mod targets are the seed's own (ATK/DEF/ACC/EVA).

name: townsfolk
function: populate the map's settlements with residents and a merchant (the economy sink)
label: townsfolk
reuse: the world-generation lever pointed at TOWN LIFE (sibling of wildlands/bestiary/armory): load_settlements reads seeds/<world>/settlements.yaml (a manifest emitted by tools/emit_map_world.py: one row per town/landmark with name/zone/level); populate_settlements grows each settlement into _FOLK_PER_TOWN peaceful residents (a trade + an ask-topic each) plus one MERCHANT with a level-banded shop of the seed's own draughts. Closes the economy: kills pay coins, the merchant is the sink.
notes: Deterministic/pure, merged into NPCS in world.py before inspect_world_links so each merchant's shop wares (real seed consumables) pass the same boot cross-check as an authored shop. Merchants sell _WARE_BANDS by settlement level; buy back at half price. Dungeons are excluded (they get guardians, not folk).

name: coinage
function: denominate the purse into a readable, tiered currency (Aethryn's ember-coin)
label: coinage
reuse: the Economy campaign's currency system (PART II): an original ember-struck coinage (Cinder->Spark->Ember->Forgemark, x100 steps) that DENOMINATES the existing persisted `coins` scalar for display without changing wealth. Coinage is a data-driven tier table (a seed can define its own coin); AETHRYN_COINAGE is the default; format()/purse() are pure. Wired into wallet, shop (render/buy/sell), and combat's kill reward.
notes: Reuse-not-replace per the campaign PRIMARY RULE: the atomic coins int stays canonical/persisted; this only formats it. Inflation control is the sinks (shops/repairs/taxes), a separate concern. Validates the tier table (base per==1, ascending, unique names/symbols).

name: delve
function: expand the map's dungeon mouths into multi-room delves with a boss ladder
label: delve
reuse: the world-generation lever pointed at DUNGEONS (sibling of wildlands/bestiary/armory): load_dungeons reads seeds/<world>/dungeons.yaml (emitted by tools/emit_map_world.py: one row per dungeon mouth); generate_delves sinks a _DEPTH-chamber descent below each mouth with foes escalating in level (make_beast, ambient trash) to a named deep BOSS (make_notable, boss-tier + lethal, out-levelling the mouth by _BOSS_BUMP); wire_delve_mouths opens each mouth `down`. The boss is armed with armory gear in world.py. Turns 16 single-room dungeons into real delves.
notes: Deterministic/pure. Merged in world.py before inspect_world_links so the new rooms + boss drops pass the same gate. Trash foes stay ambient (no bounty flood); only the deep boss mints a bounty. wire_delve_mouths skips a missing mouth room rather than failing the boot.

name: allocate
function: spend the attribute points a level-up grants (build your hero)
label: allocate
reuse: the build-agency verb: earned()/spent()/unspent() derive the point pool from level; allocate() spends into an attribute (per_stat_cap gates it); jobs.build_stats folds the allocation onto the job base so it applies across job changes; serialize()/restore() persist it (characters.allocated JSON column + Alembic c9f2e4a71d38).
notes: Derive-don't-store: unspent is earned minus spent, never a stored balance. Stamina/magic points grow the HP/MP pool immediately (_apply) and fully on restore (HP/MP recompute from the allocated stats). Loaded before bind_calling on restore.

name: artifact
function: the Maker's Signet: the Seed Owner's legendary bond, the Creator Interface borne anywhere
label: artifact
reuse: Part III of the Player Experience campaign (the Creator Artifact): a legendary owner-bound relic that opens the Creator Interface ANYWHERE and channels the Creator Workshop's read-only tools remotely (signet survey / signet activity). Modeled as the owner's inherent bond, not a takeable item, so it satisfies every can't-be-X rule (trade/steal/copy/destroy/drop) by construction. Composes with creator_workshop (the survey/activity report content was split from the station gate so both the station and the signet share it).
notes: bears_signet == is_seed_owner. Read-only functions only for now (world_survey/live_activity); mutating create/publish stay station-bound to the Workshop. A non-owner is refused ('does not know your hand').

name: gather
function: harvest crafting materials from the wilds (the maker's non-combat source)
label: gather
reuse: the crafting loop's missing SOURCE: a room may carry a `node` (Room.node, a material prototype); `gather` mints one into the player's hands, then the node renews after GATHER_COOLDOWN beats (per-player, tracked on session.gather_cooldowns, ticked by tick_gather on the world beat). gather_hint shows a node on look. The wildlands generator seeds nodes (~1 in 5 rooms; ember_shard, ore biomes yield hollow_ingot) - both real crafting inputs, so gather->craft->equip closes.
notes: Nodes are a Room field, not NPCs/items, so scaling adds negligible cost (10,691 nodes at scale 1). Per-player cooldown = an MMO node is not contested. Fails soft on an unknown material.

name: travel
function: the Waystone network: pay to cross the world (the economy's great coin sink)
label: travel
reuse: the economy's largest coin SINK + fast-travel: load_waystones reads seeds/<world>/waystones.yaml (the 14 zone hubs, emitted); travel(session,arg,stones) at a hub lists the network + fares (bare) or pays a fare (fare(level)=20+2*level cinders) and moves. Danger not cost gates the far zones. WAYSTONES loaded in world.py; wired to the travel verb (CMD-04.090).
notes: Data-driven; a seed with no waystones.yaml has no network ({} for first-forge/spiral-ascent). Fare scales with the DESTINATION level so a deep hop is a fortune; refuses off-hub, unknown hub, empty purse. Persists the move+purse.

name: feats
function: the deeds a hero has earned, derived from what they have already become
label: feats
reuse: the achievements/long-term-goals panel, built DERIVE-DON'T-STORE: a feat is a truth read live off the character's already-persisted state (level/job/subjob/order/coins/rank), never a stored flag. FEATS is a data table of (name, blurb, predicate); earned_feats/feats render earned vs locked with a next-deed nudge. No new persistence, no migration.
notes: Named `feats` to avoid the classroom `achievements` verb. Feats needing a NEW counter (foes felled, rooms walked) are a later slice; every feat here rides an existing persisted fact.

name: errands
function: generate travel side-quests across the map (side-content variety, at volume)
label: errands
reuse: the AAA-content-density quest lever, non-combat half (sibling of bounties for kills): generate_errands(settlements, destinations) posts one travel-errand per settlement, each sending the player to a DISTINCT destination (town/dungeon/hub) completed by on_enter arrival - collision-free (unique dest rooms, unlike a shared item). Flavour varies by destination kind. Folded into the quest engine via register_errands; shown on the `contracts` notice board beside bounties.
notes: Systemic, not hand-crafted: reaches quest VOLUME + a new TYPE (exploration/courier) the way bounties reach kill-volume. Reward scales with the poster's level band. is_errand() = 'errand_' prefix. aethryn: 45 errands (interleaved 16 dungeon / 14 hub / 15 town).

name: storylines
function: weave a multi-beat narrative quest chain through every zone that pairs a town with a dungeon
label: storylines
reuse: the AAA-content-density DEPTH lever (bounties/errands gave VOLUME, this gives narrative): generate_storylines(zones, settlements, dungeons) forges one three-beat chain per zone that has both a town and a dungeon - reach the dungeon (on_enter), slay its deep boss (on_defeat=<room>_deep_boss), bear word home to the town (on_enter, award_xp). Woven from the world's own geography, folded into the quest engine via register_storylines; shown on the `contracts` notice board under a `Tales:` group. Starts already afoot so it advertises its hook.
notes: Systemic, not hand-crafted (not WoW prose, but a genuine zone arc): each beat fires from a real world action. is_storyline() = 'story_' prefix; id is story_<town_room>. Reward scales with the zone's level_max (a capstone). A zone missing a town or a dungeon simply gets no tale (honest coverage).

name: relics
function: forge one signature legendary drop for every dungeon's deep boss (loot payoff)
label: relics
reuse: the AAA-content-density LOOT-PAYOFF lever (the armory gave generic gear VOLUME, this gives the memorable reward): forge_relic() builds one named legendary equippable per dungeon (iconic name drawn from the dungeon, legendary stat floor not an affix gamble, a readable `lore` line); arm_deep_bosses(dungeons, npcs) attaches each to its `<room>_deep_boss` as a GUARANTEED drop on top of the generic gear. Prototypes merge into ITEMS before the link audit.
notes: Systemic, not hand-crafted: the same dungeon always yields the same relic (deterministic, reproducible). is_relic() = 'relic_' prefix; label is relic_<dungeon_room>. Slot/stats spread by dungeon index so a region's relics vary across weapons/armour/trinkets. aethryn: 16 signature relics (one per deep boss).

name: rumors
function: seed town residents with gossip that points at the real nearby content (discovery)
label: rumors
reuse: the AAA-content-density DISCOVERY lever (townsfolk gave town life, this makes it point somewhere): seed_rumors(town_npcs, zones, dungeons) mutates each resident of a dungeon-bearing zone to add a `rumor` topic (and a woven greeting) that NAMES that dungeon and the signature relic it guards (the same name kernel.world.relics forges), so `ask <folk> about rumor` guides a player onward. Weaves the world's own geography + loot into NPC talk.
notes: Systemic, not hand-crafted: the same town always tells the same tale (deterministic; the relic name is recomputed via forge_relic with the matching dungeon index). Merchants keep to their wares (skipped). Rumour lines vary by resident index. A town in a dungeonless zone keeps its plain small talk (honest silence). aethryn: every settlement in a dungeon zone points at its dungeon + relic.

name: inscriptions
function: carve a readable lore inscription into every dungeon's deepest chamber (environmental storytelling)
label: inscriptions
reuse: the AAA-content-density ENVIRONMENTAL-STORYTELLING lever: carve_inscriptions(dungeons) places one readable, unequippable lore item in each dungeon's boss chamber (via delve.boss_chamber), its words naming the dungeon AND the relic it guards (the same name relics.forge_relic makes). Closes the discovery loop: a town rumour points here, the inscription confirms the prize, felling the boss claims it. `read <inscription>` shows the lore.
notes: Systemic, not hand-crafted: the same dungeon always bears the same words (deterministic; relic name recomputed with the matching dungeon index). is_inscription() = 'inscription_' prefix; label is inscription_<dungeon_room>. Merged into ITEMS before the link audit (rooms are the delve chambers). aethryn: 16 inscriptions (one per dungeon). Exposed delve.boss_chamber() so the label isn't hardcoded.

name: spine
function: forge the world's main-road quest: one guided journey through the zones in level order
label: spine
reuse: the AAA-content-density THROUGH-LINE lever: forge_spine(zones) lays one campaign quest (the Forgeward Road) whose beats are entering each zone's hub (first room) in level order -- the main quest that orients a new player and pulls them across the map from the starting band to the endgame. Lives in the `quest` log, not the notice board (the spine the side-content hangs on). Folded into the engine via register_spine.
notes: Systemic, not hand-crafted: the same world always lays the same road (deterministic, ordered by level_min then level_max). SPINE_ID = 'spine_forgeward_road' (one per world); is_spine() checks it. Reward scales with the last zone's level_max, granted on reaching the final zone. Returns None for a world with < 2 zones. aethryn: a 14-zone road, Veridia (1-30) to The Voidscar (250-300).

name: delve_sets
function: forge a matched gear set per dungeon, dropped across its delve (collect-by-clearing)
label: delve_sets
reuse: the AAA-content-density ITEMIZATION-SET lever: forge_delve_sets(dungeons, npcs) forges three themed armour pieces per dungeon (head/body/arm, distinct slots), hangs one on each of the delve's three trash foes as a guaranteed drop, and declares a GearSet whose bonus fires when all three are worn -- so clearing the whole descent earns a set (the boss relic is a separate prize). Reuses the existing set-bonus engine via new gearsets.register_sets. Named for the dungeon (relics.iconic_word).
notes: Systemic, not hand-crafted: the same dungeon always yields the same set (deterministic). is_delve_set_piece() = 'delveset_' prefix; set label is delveset_<dungeon_room>. Pieces are epic-rarity; bonus (DEF/EVA) scales with the dungeon level. A shallow delve (< 2 trash foes) forms no set. Made relics._iconic_word public (iconic_word) so the set name matches the relic. aethryn: 16 dungeon sets.

name: landmarks
function: raise a readable monument in every zone's hub (surface storytelling)
label: landmarks
reuse: the AAA-content-density SURFACE-STORYTELLING lever (the twin of inscriptions' depths lore): raise_landmarks(zones, dungeons) places one readable, unequippable monument item in each zone's hub (its first room), its words naming the region, its recommended level band, and any dungeon within. So arriving in a region reads as an arrival, and the monument points a player onward. `read <monument>` shows it.
notes: Systemic, not hand-crafted: the same zone always raises the same monument (deterministic). is_landmark() = 'landmark_' prefix; label is landmark_<hub_room>. Merged into ITEMS after the world is assembled (load_zones already proved the hubs exist, so no link-audit needed). A hubless zone is skipped; two zones sharing a hub keep one monument. aethryn: 14 monuments (one per zone).

name: wardens
function: name each dungeon's deep boss for its dungeon so the whole content web names one foe
label: wardens
reuse: the AAA-content-density COHERENCE lever: name_wardens(dungeons, npcs) renames each `<room>_deep_boss` from a random forge-name to a titled warden of its own dungeon ('the Warden of The Black Hollow') and re-keys its keywords (title / dungeon word / warden / boss), so the rumour's 'terror', the inscription's 'keeper', the relic 'torn from' the dungeon, the bounty, and the foe itself all name one individual. Stats/tier unchanged: identity only. Wired BEFORE register_bounties so the bounty reads the new name.
notes: Systemic, not hand-crafted: the same dungeon always crowns the same warden (deterministic; title by dungeon index over Warden/Keeper/Devourer/Sentinel/Herald/Scourge). Uses relics.iconic_word for the keyword. A dungeon whose deep boss is absent is skipped. aethryn: 16 named wardens.

name: boss_phases
function: give boss fights a second gear: a wounded boss enrages and hits harder
label: boss_phases
reuse: the AAA-content ENCOUNTER-MECHANIC lever (the first meatier system past the bounded generators): boss_phase(npc, raw) is combat's phase hook -- when a boss-tier foe drops to ENRAGE_AT (30% HP) its outgoing blow scales by ENRAGE_MULT (1.5x) and the room hears an enrage line ONCE. Deterministic (a HP threshold, not a die) and self-healing (the flag clears above the line, so a rematch re-announces). Additive: a non-boss or a healthy boss strikes exactly as before, so normal combat is byte-identical.
notes: Wired into combat._resolve_npc_blow right after npc_strike_power, before the weaken fold. is_boss() = tier=='boss'; is_enraged() reads the runtime 'enraged' flag. Keyed on tier=='boss' so the training dummy, elites, and every existing combat test (non-boss foes) are untouched. This is the smallest real boss mechanic; phase 3 / special attacks are a later pass.

name: cull
function: generate zone-scoped 'fell N of a kind' contracts at volume (the MMO's staple quest)
label: cull
reuse: the QUEST-VOLUME lever (archetype 1 of the 'WoW amounts of quests' campaign): generate_culls(zones) posts one 'cull N of a kind' per zone x each creature TYPE of its biome x count-tier (6/12/20). Modeled as an N-step chain (one step per kill) so it needs NO counter engine -- the state is the tally, persisted like any quest. Uses a NEW `on_cull` quest trigger (seed.QuestStep) fired by combat per keyword, SCOPED to the kill's zone via cull.scope_key(zone,kind) so kills only count where they happen (honest distinctness, not one quest cloned per place). Summarised on the `contracts` board (too many to itemise), counted (not listed) in the `quest` log.
notes: is_cull() = 'cull_' prefix; id = cull_<zone_label>_<kind>_<count>. Combat fires on_event('cull', scope_key(zone_of(location), kw)) per keyword on defeat. Bestiary.classes_for_biome() made public for the cullable types. aethryn: 336 culls (28 zones x 4 types x 3 tiers), total quests 205 -> 541. Next archetypes: forage (gather N), delivery (carry A->B).

name: forage
function: generate zone-scoped 'gather N of a material' contracts (the non-combat volume archetype)
label: forage
reuse: the QUEST-VOLUME lever (archetype 2, the non-combat twin of cull): generate_forages(zones) posts one 'gather N of a material' per zone x material its biome yields x count-tier (5/10). Same N-step-chain (no counter) and same cull.scope_key zone-scoping; the gather action fires on_event('forage', scope_key(zone_of(location), material)) on a successful harvest. New `on_forage` quest trigger (seed.QuestStep). wildlands.gatherable_materials() made public. Summarised on the `contracts` board via the shared quest._tally; counted (not listed) in the `quest` log.
notes: is_forage() = 'forage_' prefix; id = forage_<zone_label>_<material>_<count>. Materials today: ember_shard (all biomes) + hollow_ingot (ore biomes) -- modest volume until more materials land. aethryn: 88 forages, total quests 541 -> 629. Next: delivery (carry A->B), then crank kins/materials/tiers toward thousands.

name: quest_archetypes
function: the data-driven catalog of quest archetypes the world generates
label: quest_archetypes
reuse: the FRAMEWORK for the content-generation campaign (slice 1 of the /home/josh/Projects/prompt brief): the Quest Archetype Library. One frozen Archetype record per shipped generator (spine/storyline/bounty/cull/forage/errand) naming purpose, narrative role, gameplay loop, success, rewards, replay, and scope, beside the generator's is_<x> predicate. classify(quest_id) maps any live quest to its archetype key (or AUTHORED). Turns ad-hoc generators into a legible, extensible catalog; a new archetype is a new record. Design doc: docs/quest_archetypes.md (with the roadmap of the ~40 further archetypes from the prompt).
notes: Data, not behavior -- the generators stay where they live; this names/organises them. The completeness test proves every quest a booted world posts partitions into exactly one archetype (or authored), so no archetype ships uncatalogued. CATALOG is ordered specific-before-broad (classify = first match). AUTHORED is the fallback (hand-written quest.yaml + the built-in contract), not a catalog entry.

name: delivery
function: generate 'carry a parcel from town A to town B' contracts (a courier archetype)
label: delivery
reuse: a new quest ARCHETYPE (content campaign slice 1, for variety alongside the volume): generate_deliveries(settlements) returns (quest specs, parcel items). Each town consigns a parcel to its level-adjacent trade-partner; the quest is a two-beat arc -- take the parcel (on_take matches the parcel's prototype, since a placed seed item is its own prototype) then arrive at the destination (on_enter, award_xp). world.py places the parcels at their source towns and folds the specs via the new generic quest.register_specs(). Cataloged in quest_archetypes.
notes: is_delivery() = 'delivery_' prefix; parcels are 'parcel_<source_room>'. _routes pairs settlements sorted by level, each to the next (wrapping), so every town gets one delivery to a distinct neighbour. aethryn: 45 deliveries + 45 parcels, total quests 1565 -> 1610. Added quest.register_specs() (public _fold_in) for archetypes whose generator also mints world-placed artifacts.

name: dungeon_crawl
function: generate 'descend to the heart of a dungeon' contracts (an exploration archetype)
label: dungeon_crawl
reuse: a new quest ARCHETYPE (content campaign slice 1, exploration): generate_crawls(dungeons) posts one two-beat descent per dungeon -- cross the mouth (on_enter the mouth room) then reach the deep boss's chamber (on_enter delve.boss_chamber(mouth), award_xp). Rewards DEPTH itself; the boss's fall and relic are a separate prize. Reuses the delve geography + on_enter, no new machinery. Cataloged in quest_archetypes.
notes: is_dungeon_crawl() = 'crawl_' prefix; id = crawl_<mouth>. Distinct from storyline (which slays the boss + returns home): the crawl pays for reaching the depths at all. aethryn: 16 crawls, total quests 1610 -> 1626.

name: zone_story
function: assemble a zone's scattered content into one story dossier (the Zone Story Framework)
label: zone_story
reuse: the ZONE STORY FRAMEWORK (content campaign slice 2, Part II): every zone already carries its pieces across six generators (tale/dungeon+warden/monument/inscription/cull+forage board); assemble(zone_label) gathers them from the LIVE world into one ZoneStory (read-only, derived, invents nothing), and region_view(session) renders the dossier of the zone the player stands in -- its history, dangers, and opportunities at a glance (the `region` verb, CMD-04.092). Added quest.all_ids()/hook_of() so it surveys the board without touching the private registry.
notes: Composes, never replaces: a zone's story is exactly the sum of its filed content. Finds the dungeon by the room whose <room>_deep_boss exists; the settlement by its _merchant; lore from the landmark/inscription items; cull/forage counts by the zone-scoped id prefix. The completeness test pins that a dungeon-bearing zone reports its full depths (warden -> inscription).

name: respawn
function: the world's respawn philosophy: a catalog of its policies + the dynamic-spawn primitive
label: respawn
reuse: the RESPAWN FRAMEWORK (content campaign slice 3, Part IV): one RespawnPolicy record per respawn behavior in the game (zone_item_reset / gather_node / training_dummy / lethal_recover), naming what respawns, its trigger, cadence, and the gameplay REASON it exists, plus the module.attr that implements it. Carries pick_room(candidates, weights, rng) -- the pure, seedable dynamic-spawn primitive (weighted site choice from a pool, '' for empty) the dynamic policies build on ('avoid static, predictable locations'). render_policies() summarises the philosophy. Doc: docs/respawn.md.
notes: The completeness test pins that every policy's lives_in=(module, attr) still resolves, so the philosophy can't drift loose from the code. SPAWN_RNG is a seedable module RNG (runtime variety, not world-gen which stays deterministic). NEXT (slice 3b): wire pick_room live -- an opt-in item spawn_pool the zone reset draws from (the wandering pickup), then rare-spawn rotation.

name: climate
function: the world's season and weather, turning on the beat (the world-sim layer's clock)
label: climate
reuse: the WORLD-SIMULATION layer, slice 1 (content campaign slice 4, Part IV): season_of(beat)/weather_of(beat) derive the world's season (spring/summer/autumn/winter, 40 beats each) and weather (a season's pool, holding 7 beats) PURELY from the world beat, so any two readers agree and a test can name the day. climate_line renders it; the `weather` verb (CMD-04.093) shows it. tick_climate rides the beat beside tick_zones. The seam future 'seasonal availability' / 'weather-dependent spawns' read (respawn.pick_room weights); the world-sim layer factions/reputation ride next.
notes: The MATH is pure and total (tested without booting a world); the beat counter (_beat) is runtime, like the zone beats -- a fresh boot starts the year at day 0 (a documented limitation, no persistence yet). tick_climate/weather_view are silent/read-only, so no existing look/combat test moves.

name: factions
function: the standing between the Orders: who is allied, who is rival (faction conflicts)
label: factions
reuse: the WORLD-SIM layer's FACTION CONFLICTS (content campaign slice 4, Part II 'faction conflicts'): a relationship model OVER the existing Orders (kernel.world.orders), never a replacement. Two axes -- the hand that builds (making+gathering) vs the memory+shield that endure (warcraft+knowing) allied, the cross-cutting tensions rival. stance(a,b) = self/allied/rival/neutral (symmetric); relations_of(order) = (allies, rivals); render_factions(sworn) shows the politics of the Row, marking the reader's Order. The `factions` verb (CMD-04.094). The seam a faction-gated spawn or faction storyline pulls next (stance(mine, theirs)).
notes: Pure data over the 4 Orders; no new allegiance, no second source of truth (Forger still swears one Order via `join`). Reputation (a numeric standing) is a later slice; this is the conflict MODEL. _ALLIED/_RIVAL are unordered frozenset pairs; every un-named pairing is neutral.

name: professions
function: the maker's trades: skill tracks leveled by gathering and crafting (persisted per hero)
label: professions
notes: professions.advance: gather/craft what a trade governs to earn practice; level derives from it. Slice 1b of the Crafting Campaign.

name: reputation
function: a hero's numeric standing with each Order, banded into tiers, over the faction model
label: reputation
notes: reputation.grant: the single earn door (deeds raise/lower standing, spilling over allies/rivals). Roadmap #2.

name: afflictions
function: harmful statuses the PLAYER suffers: damage-over-time and daze (the foe-side mirror)
label: afflictions
notes: tick_afflictions ages player DoT/daze on the world beat; maybe_inflict is the NPC-blow door. Unblocks encounter depth (#4).

name: boss_specials
function: a telegraphed boss SPECIAL: an enraged boss winds up (readable), then unleashes hard
label: boss_specials
notes: maybe_begin_charge telegraphs (no blow), unleash spikes the next blow + guaranteed affliction. Encounter depth (#4).

name: navigation
function: the world as a graph: shortest room paths + reachability, native-accelerated (Rust/PyO3)
label: navigation
notes: Python-first NavGraph with an identical-interface Rust fallback (native/codeforge_nav); parity-pinned. First polyglot organ.

name: edge
function: a transparent TCP edge proxy in front of the gateway, Go-accelerated (goroutines)
label: edge
reuse: a byte-transparent connection front door; raise the thread-per-connection ceiling for any line-based TCP service
notes: Python-first EdgeProxy with an identical-behaviour Go fallback (native/edge, goroutine-per-connection); parity-pinned. First service organ (out-of-process, ADR-0011).

name: telemetry
function: the protocol spine: one typed frame contract, json + protobuf codecs
label: telemetry
reuse: a language-neutral typed wire contract (proto/telemetry.proto) for any cross-language service; the keystone the polyglot organs share
notes: JSON reference codec (always) + optional protobuf codec from one .proto compiled to Python + Go; cross-language byte-parity pinned by tests/test_telemetry.py via native/spine/xcheck. The protocol spine (ADR-0012).

name: analytics
function: SQL analytics over the character archive (leaderboard, spread, wealth)
label: analytics
reuse: set-shaped reports (rank / group / aggregate) as portable SQL over any archive; a template for pushing analytics into the database engine
notes: Python reference + identical-result SQL query (window functions/GROUP BY/aggregates) per report; parity pinned by tests/test_analytics.py; portable SQLite + PostgreSQL (Postgres-gated test). Adds no dependency (stdlib sqlite3 + approved SQLAlchemy/psycopg). The SQL analytics organ (ADR-0013).

name: condition
function: a Lens on the hero's present state: vital pools, afflictions, sworn standing
label: condition
reuse: the at-a-glance transient-state view pattern: compose fast-changing session facts into one read-only projection, distinct from the persistent record sheet
notes: Backs the `condition` verb (CMD-04.098); wires afflictions.render_afflictions (a tested renderer that had no verb) into a player-reachable readout. Read-only projection (state is canonical). Roadmap: status view.

name: party
function: the fellowship: a transient leader-led band of heroes with its own chat channel
label: party
reuse: the transient cohort primitive: own membership in a module registry keyed by player id, deliver to the set via events.announce_to, persist nothing; a guild is its persisted big sibling
notes: Backs the `party` (CMD-04.099) + `psay` (CMD-04.100) verbs. All state in the module registry (never persisted, dissolves on logout via on_disconnect, hooked into both gateway teardowns). members_in_room is the seam shared combat/XP will read. Foundation for dungeons/raids/social (the AAA-scorecard's deepest gap).

name: party_rewards
function: shared combat's reward half: a felled foe's advancement spreads across the co-located party
label: party_rewards
reuse: the shared-reward seam: distribute a progression award across a cohort via a data-driven SHARE_POLICY, awarding through the same path a solo action uses; an alternative economy (even-split, diminishing returns) swaps the policy without touching callers
notes: Hangs off combat.land_hit's single kill/reward seam (one lazy call), so combat stays untouched. Reads party.members_in_room; awards XP/JP/TP to present mates via progression_awards (coins/loot NOT split -- loot rules are a separate feature). SHARE_POLICY='full' (tag-credit: grouping is purely rewarding). Extension: even-split policy, shared threat/aggro, loot rules.

name: trade
function: a safe, atomic player-to-player swap of goods and coin between two co-located heroes
label: trade
reuse: the atomic two-party exchange pattern: validate all stakes on both sides, then apply in one pass (validate-all-then-apply) so a swap can never duplicate, lose, or overpay
notes: First player-to-player economy loop, built on per-player inventory (#569). Transient module registry keyed by player id (never persisted); items move by carrier-tag reassignment, coin by the purse scalar. Nothing moves until the atomic execute, so cancel/logout unwind cleanly. on_disconnect hooked into both gateways. Verb: trade (CMD-04.101). Foundation for a market/auction.

name: party_loot
function: shared combat's loot half: a party's drops are awarded to co-located mates by round-robin
label: party_loot
reuse: the fair-distribution seam: a data-driven LOOT_POLICY rotates a shared resource across a cohort; need-vs-greed / master-looter swap the policy without touching combat
notes: Hangs off combat._spawn_loot's single seam (one lazy call); reads party.members_in_room, moves a just-spawned drop by carrier-tag reassignment (per-player inventory). Solo/unpartied loot unchanged (falls to floor). Round-robin turn keyed by party leader. Companion to party_rewards (shared XP). Extension: need-greed rolls, master looter.

name: guild
function: a PERSISTED player organization: a named guild with ranks and a chat channel
label: guild
reuse: the persisted-membership organization: durable member+rank columns as the source of truth, live sessions mirroring them, with a rank ladder gating governance actions
notes: The party's durable big sibling. Guild+guild_rank are additive character columns (migration e7a3c1b5f2d8); the CharacterStore gained members_of_guild + set_guild so a guild reads its full roster and reaches offline members (disband). Every change writes through immediately (online via save_character, offline via set_guild) so the persisted roster stays authoritative. Ranks member<officer<leader. Verbs guild (CMD-04.102) + gsay (CMD-04.103). Extension: guild bank, MOTD, guild quests.

name: guild_store
function: persistence for a guild's own record (its shared treasury): one row per guild
label: guild_store
reuse: a small guild-LEVEL persistence adapter (a treasury row): the pattern for any org-level state distinct from per-member columns; direct SQL, no auth/merge-save law needed
notes: The guilds table (GuildRow: name PK, coins; migration f1b9d3e6c284). Created on found(), dropped on disband(). ensure/remove/coins/adjust; adjust floors the balance at 0. Backs the guild bank (guild deposit/withdraw/bank). Extension: MOTD, guild level, a guild item vault (needs loose-item persistence first).

name: mail
function: asynchronous letters between heroes: send now, read later (reaches an offline hero)
label: mail
reuse: the async-message primitive: validated send + bounded inbox + read/delete over a persisted store; the pattern for any offline-delivered notification
notes: The social layer's patient channel (vs party/guild live chat). Sends to any real character (validated via the character store, online or not); nudges the recipient if online. Body <= MAX_BODY, inbox <= MAX_INBOX (bounds flooding); body sanitized by the transport on read. Verb mail (CMD-04.104).

name: mail_store
function: persistence for stored letters: send, inbox (newest first), count, mark-read, delete
label: mail_store
reuse: a per-recipient message queue over a table with an autoincrement id; delete scoped to the owner so no id-guessing across inboxes
notes: The mail table (MailRow: id autoincrement, recipient[indexed], sender, body, sent_utc, read; migration a3e7c9b1d5f4). A Letter value object crosses the boundary (no ORM leak). Direct SQL, lazy import (EXP-003).

name: textmatch
function: fuzzy string matching: Levenshtein edit distance + the nearest candidate
label: textmatch
reuse: any 'did you mean ...?' / typo-tolerant lookup: nearest command, item, exit, or label by edit distance
notes: Hardware Store part; pure-Python levenshtein_py reference + an identical-interface hand-written C accelerator (native/textkernel, raw CPython API, ~53x); parity + hypothesis-pinned. WIRED as the engine tick's 'did you mean' nudge (forge._did_you_mean). In-process kernel under ADR-0010.

name: cohort
function: a transient membership group: a leader-led band formed/joined/left/disbanded via a registry
label: cohort
reuse: the transient membership-group primitive: a member->group registry with leadership handoff and a size cap; a party/guild/chat-room/raid all layer domain on this core
notes: Hardware Store part harvested from the game's party/shared-reward/loot systems (proven by 3 uses). party.py is its adapter (bolts invites+chat+logout cleanup on). Framework-free, fail-loud, no persistence. The guild will be its next consumer.

name: scripting
function: a sandboxed Lua interpreter for safe user/creator scripts
label: scripting
reuse: embed a safe scripting language: a deny-by-default whitelist env + a bounded-execution hook, for any host that wants user extensibility
notes: Embeds real Lua (via lupa) behind a deny-by-default sandbox (no os/io/require/load/debug; a debug-hook instruction budget bounds loops). OPTIONAL: absent -> scripting_available() False, game untouched. Evidence is the safety suite, not a benchmark. WIRED as the owner-only @script console (CMD-10.025). Embedded scripting organ (ADR-0014).

name: friends
function: a hero's personal, one-directional friends list; shows who is online
label: friends
reuse: the personal-roster primitive: a validated, bounded, per-owner list of labels persisted as a comma-joined column; the pattern for any user-curated watch list
notes: The social layer's quiet corner (vs shared party/guild). One-directional: your list is yours; adding does not touch the other hero. Names validated against the character store (a friend may be offline); list <= MAX_FRIENDS. serialize/restore mirror the professions/reputation columns; characters imports it lazily-free via a top-level import while friends imports characters lazily (no cycle). Verbs friend (CMD-04.105) + friends (CMD-04.106).

name: chat
function: the world channel: one line heard by every hero online right now
label: chat
reuse: the broadcast-channel primitive: validated, membership-wide delivery over the online roster; the pattern for any world-wide or zone-wide live announcement
notes: The social layer's widest voice (vs party->band, guild->order, mail->one offline hero). Transient, moves no world state. Speaker must be named + in the world; message non-empty. Delivers via events.announce_to(roster(), exclude=self); offline heroes skipped. Rate-limit + opt-out mute are documented extension points, not built. Verb chat (CMD-04.107).

name: inns
function: give every settlement an inn interior and its keeper (a town's twin of the delve)
label: inns
reuse: the interior-generator primitive: per site, emit one linked interior room + a peaceful host and open the hub's exit into it (raise/wire pair mirrors the delve generator); the pattern for shops, homes, guildhalls
notes: Additive world generator. raise_inns(configs)->(rooms,npcs): one inn room f'{hub}_inn' (exit out->hub) + an innkeeper per settlement. wire_inn_doors opens each hub's `in` exit into its inn, in place (skips a hub absent from the world, like wire_delve_mouths). Merged before the link audit. Composes with the social layer (a gathering point for parties + world chat). Deterministic per settlement.

name: stores
function: a general store off every town plaza: the two-way market for raw materials
label: stores
reuse: the interior-market primitive: per site, emit a linked interior + a vendor NPC with a two-way shop and open the hub's exit into it (raise/wire pair, like inns/delve); the pattern for any specialized vendor building
notes: Additive world generator, the inn's counterpart. raise_stores(configs, known_items)->(rooms,npcs): one store room f'{hub}_store' (exit out->hub) + a provisioner per settlement whose two-way shop BUYS raw materials (the coin SOURCE gatherers lacked) and SELLS them on at 2x (crafters short a material). Buy list filtered to materials present in the loaded seed (herbs canonical from wildlands._BIOME_HERB) so the boot cross-check always passes. wire_store_doors opens each hub's `market` exit (reached via `go market`). Merged before the link audit.

name: maintenance_mode
function: a runtime gate that closes the forge to non-staff for an orderly shutdown
label: maintenance_mode
reuse: the runtime-ops-flag primitive: a transient process-lifetime gate a driver reads at the door and an admin verb writes; the pattern for any 'close the service' control
notes: Infrastructure spec Phase 0. Transient (not persisted; a restart clears it, which is correct). enable(reason)/disable()/is_on()/reason(). The gateway front desk turns away sub-wizard logins with the reason while on; the @maintenance verb (CMD-10.026, owner) toggles it and broadcasts. Distinct from the existing `maintenance` change-log verb (kernel/maintenance.py).

name: loose_store
function: persistence for a hero's loose inventory (their bag survives logout) - Keystone A
label: loose_store
reuse: the item-instance-persistence primitive: snapshot (prototype + rolled name/mods/rarity) a live item into a row and re-clone it back; the keystone the auction house, mail attachments, and a guild item-vault build on (items with a non-player owner)
notes: Keystone A slice 1. save(owner, snapshots) replaces a hero's whole bag (delete-then-insert) so storage always mirrors the live bag; load(owner) returns snapshots to re-clone. Direct SQL on the loose_items table (ArchiveBase, migration d4b8f1a2c6e9), lazy ORM import off the hot path. Domain glue in characters.py: _snapshot_loose (items_in(carrier) minus equipped), _clear_carrier before restore (no reconnect dup), _snapshot_item/_reclone_item shared with equipped gear.

name: bank
function: a hero's personal vault: deposit/withdraw items that wait in storage between sessions
label: bank
reuse: the non-player-owner storage pattern (Phase 2): move a live item into storage under a namespaced owner and back, via loose_store.stow/take + snapshot_item/reclone_item; the shape guild vaults, mail attachments, and the auction house all extend
notes: Infra spec Phase 2 slice 1 - the first thing Keystone A unlocks. deposit(snapshot->stow, drop the instance)/withdraw(take->reclone into carrier)/render, owner key vault:<player> on the loose_items table. Refuses depositing worn gear. Item-level loose_store.stow/take/contents added as the twin of the whole-bag save/load; characters.snapshot_item/reclone_item made public for reuse.

name: scheduler
function: a timed-job registry the world beat drains (deferred work on the game clock)
label: scheduler
reuse: the deferred-work primitive: register a callback for a future BEAT (one-shot or recurring), the tick drains it - deterministic, no wall-clock, no background thread; for auction expiry, timed world events, buff expiry
notes: Infra spec Phase 0/2.4, the auction house's prerequisite. schedule(due_beat, run, every=0)/run_due(now_beat)->fired/pending/clear; tick(session) drains at climate.now() and composes into the beat AFTER tick_climate advances it. A job that raises is DROPPED (never crashes the tick). In-memory: work that must survive a restart re-registers a sweep at boot over its own persisted rows.

name: auction
function: the marketplace: list an item for coin, buy another's, expiry mails the unsold back
label: auction
reuse: the escrow-marketplace pattern: an item held out of the world under storage, sold atomically with coin credited to an offline seller, returned by a scheduler sweep; the Phase-2 economy capstone
notes: Infra spec Phase 2 slice 4. list_item escrows a carried item (snapshot->auction_store, drop instance, expiry=climate.now()+AUCTION_BEATS); browse renders live listings; buy pays (session.coins or store.add_coins for an offline seller), atomically removes the listing (auction_store.buy) so it can't be double-sold, and reclones the item to the buyer; sweep_expired mails lapsed items back via mail attachments; register_sweep arms the recurring scheduler job at world assembly. GOTCHA: list matches by item KEYWORD not prototype.

name: auction_store
function: persistence for the auction house's escrowed listings (item snapshot + price + expiry)
label: auction_store
reuse: the escrow-storage adapter: a Listing value object over an auction_listings row; create/active/get/buy(atomic remove)/expired/remove; the storage twin of loose_store for a marketplace
notes: auction_listings table (AuctionRow, ArchiveBase, migration f6a2d9b3e8c1), seller+expiry indexed. buy() removes and returns a listing in ONE transaction so two buyers can never both win it. Lazy ORM off the hot path.

name: audit
function: a tamper-evident, hash-chained log of admin + economy actions (who did what)
label: audit
reuse: the accountability-log primitive: append(who, what, detail) to a hash-chained JSONL ledger a live server can be held to and an incident reconstructed from; the observability backbone bans + economy inspection feed
notes: Infra spec Phase 3. Built on the hashchain shelf part: record(actor, action, detail, ts=None) appends a sealed entry (best-effort: an unwritable path never aborts the action); tail(limit) reads recent (verifies the chain, raises on tamper); verify() checks it end to end. Writers: ranks.grant (admin) + auction.buy (economy). Verb @audit (CMD-10.027, owner) + @audit verify. Path CODEFORGE_AUDIT (default audit.jsonl at repo root, git-ignored; conftest quarantines to tmp).

name: bans
function: moderation: a banned character is refused at the login gate (persisted)
label: bans
reuse: the persisted-block primitive: ban/unban/is_banned/reason/all over a keyed table, checked by a driver at the door; the moderation twin of the transient maintenance gate and the address ledger
notes: Infra spec Phase 3. bans table (BanRow, migration a7d3c9f1b4e2). ban(name, reason, moderator)/unban/is_banned/reason/all_bans, direct SQL lazy off the hot path. The TCP gateway front desk refuses a banned hero (outranks maintenance + even a wizard's rank). Verbs @ban/@unban (CMD-10.028/029, wizard+) drop an online target (session.alive=False) and record to the audit log; @bans (CMD-10.030) lists.

name: metrics
function: a live-ops snapshot of the world read from storage (population + economy health)
label: metrics
reuse: the ops-snapshot primitive: one read-only projection of counts + sums an operator watches, from SQL aggregates (not row loads), plus the players-online figure off the bus-fed presence roster
notes: Infra spec Phase 3 + Phase-4 roster fold-in. snapshot()->{characters, players_online, coins_in_circulation (purse+guild treasuries), guild_treasuries, guilds, auction_listings, mail_in_flight, bans}; the stored figures via func.count/sum, players_online via presence.count() (the bus-fed roster, cross-process once a broker is set). render() labels it. Verb @metrics (CMD-10.031, owner). The concurrent-player count the panel could not name before the bus now exists.

name: bus
function: a publish/subscribe seam: the network backing the event bus grows into (Phase 4)
label: bus
reuse: the one true multi-process seam: a MessageBus Protocol (publish/subscribe/unsubscribe) callers go through, an InProcessBus default identical to a direct call, and set_bus to inject a broker adapter (Redis/socket) unchanged; a fake satisfies it with no network so CI never touches a broker
notes: Infra spec Phase 4. The step from one process to many: today the event bus delivers only to this process's connections. MessageBus is the seam; InProcessBus is the single-process default (synchronous, behaviour-identical); a network adapter implements the same Protocol and set_bus swaps it in with no caller change. A raising subscriber is isolated (one bad handler never breaks a publish). First rider: presence.

name: presence
function: who is online, maintained across the bus so any process can read the live roster (Phase 4)
label: presence
reuse: the shared-roster primitive: mark_online/mark_offline announce onto the bus, online()/count() read a set folded from those announcements; one process today, cross-process the day a broker is injected -- the concurrent-player count metrics could not name before the bus
notes: Infra spec Phase 4. The first rider on the message bus. The gateway announces a named hero online after login and offline on teardown; every subscribing process folds it into a shared online set. reconnect() re-subscribes after a bus swap. A malformed frame never corrupts the roster; a double-online does not double-count. Fed through the bus, so a network adapter makes the same set cross-process with no caller change.

name: broker
function: the stdlib pub/sub broker the bus fans across processes (Phase 4)
label: broker
reuse: the network backing behind the MessageBus seam without a dependency: a line-delimited-JSON protocol (encode_frame/decode_frame) + a transport-agnostic Broker that fans a publish to every subscriber of a topic + a thin ThreadingTCPServer daemon; provable with a fake client (no socket) and a socketpair (no port)
notes: Infra spec Phase 4. No Redis: our own architecture is the spine. encode_frame/decode_frame are the pure wire protocol (sub/unsub/pub); Broker.on_frame routes, _fan pushes to every subscribed Client (anything with send(bytes)) including the sender (its delivery handler needs the echo), drop() removes a disconnected client, topics() is the ops health read. serve() is a thin StreamRequestHandler over the tested Broker; port 0 binds ephemeral for tests. A dead client never breaks the fan-out; a garbled frame never drops a connection.

name: socket_bus
function: the MessageBus adapter that rides a socket to the broker (Phase 4)
label: socket_bus
reuse: the network implementation of the bus seam: a SocketBus satisfying the MessageBus Protocol over a socket to the broker (publish writes a frame, subscribe registers a local handler + tells the broker, a reader thread turns the fan-out back into handler calls), injected with bus.set_bus so announce_to/push_gmcp/presence reach every process with no caller change
notes: Infra spec Phase 4. connect(host, port) opens one. The one behaviour difference from InProcessBus: delivery is a round trip (publish -> broker -> reader -> handler), so a message to a player on THIS process comes back through the broker too -- the price of one shared roster; tests poll with a deadline. A dropped broker connection never crashes a publish; a bad handler never breaks delivery; close() is idempotent. Proven over socketpair (no port) + once over the serve() daemon on loopback.

name: threat
function: who a foe wants to hit: a per-NPC aggro table (the trinity's tank seam)
label: threat
reuse: the aggro primitive that makes the tank real: a per-foe threat map (add on damage/heal/taunt, top_target picks the highest-threat present hero, taunt spikes it, drop/clear on leave/defeat) so a foe strikes the hero holding its attention instead of whoever acted last
notes: The missing half of the holy trinity. combat.land_hit adds threat = damage dealt (and clears the table when a foe is felled/reassembles); aggression.menace targets threat.top_target(nid, fighters-in-room) instead of the acting session, pushing the blow to the victim while the room sees the StrikeFrame. top_target only considers PRESENT heroes, so a departed hero's stale entry never mis-targets. taunt(nid, player, present) sets the taunter one above the current top (the tank's lever); heal-generated threat + the taunt ability (kind 'taunt') shipped alongside.

name: lockouts
function: daily reset markers, so endgame rewards a return, not a grind
label: lockouts
reuse: the daily-cap primitive: a per-hero {key -> UTC date} ledger with claim (true on the first claim of the day, then false) so a repeatable activity's BONUS pays once per day; the period boundary is a date passed in (no wall-clock in pure logic), persisted on the character record
notes: Endgame's first lever against 'infinitely farmable, no diminishing returns'. session.lockouts persists via a new characters.lockouts JSON column (migration b8e4f1c2d3a9). combat.land_hit calls _daily_boss_bounty on a boss (tier=='boss') defeat: lockouts.claim(session, 'boss:<nid>', today_utc()) pays BOSS_BOUNTY_MULT x the coin drop on the day's first kill, base only after. The boss still reassembles + is farmable; only the bounty is capped. today_utc() reads the clock at the edge (monkeypatchable); deserialize tolerates a blank/garbled ledger (a lost lockout never locks a hero out).

name: roaming
function: ambient NPCs that drift between rooms on the world's beat (world life)
label: roaming
reuse: the ambient-movement primitive: the peaceful twin of aggression on the same beat -- a seed `wander` NPC drifts room to room near the player (out through an exit, or in from next door), so a static world breathes; deterministic under a seeded RNG, reindexed once per beat
notes: The 'NPCs don't move' gap. roam(session) runs in the beat chain after menace; scoped to the player's room + its neighbours (bounded cost). A `wander` NPC in the room may leave via a random exit; a wanderer next door may amble in (at most one per exit). ROAM_CHANCE gates the drift (1-in-N per beat). Seed-gated to PEACEFUL NPCs (wander + aggressive is refused loud -- a foe must not flee a fight it opened). Seeded on three aethryn townsfolk. reindex_npcs() once, only if something moved.

name: durability
function: gear wears and breaks; repair is the economy's coin sink (game)
label: durability
reuse: the coin-sink primitive the economy lacked: per-instance gear durability (wear on use, broken at 0 = no mods) + repair for coins, so a faucet-heavy economy finally drains; persists on the one snapshot_item shape worn gear + the bag both ride, so wear survives logout
notes: The 'no coin sink' gap. Durability lives on the gear instance (items.ITEMS[iid]['durability'], full when absent - old saves upgrade clean). combat._wear_gear dulls the weapon on a landed player strike + dents the body on a landed foe blow; equipment.equipped_modifiers skips a broken (0) piece so it grants no mods until mended; the `mend` verb (CMD-04.111) -> repair_session charges REPAIR_COST_PER_POINT per point and refuses loud when short. Non-gear items never wear. Persists via characters.snapshot_item/reclone_item (worn gear + bag), so you cannot repair by relogging.

name: tutorial
function: a state-driven onboarding ladder: tell a new hero the next step (game)
label: tutorial
reuse: the onboarding primitive: next_step(session) reads the hero's live state and names the single next thing to do (pick a calling -> learn to fight -> gear up -> world open), so guidance is always current and never a scripted rail; greeting() nudges a brand-new hero once and never nags a veteran
notes: The 'no tutorial' gap. next_step is a ladder off session.job/level/equipped. The `tutorial` verb (CMD-04.112) surfaces the current step any time; gateway._front_desk fires greeting() once on a fresh character's first scene (gated on no-job so an established hero is never nudged). Distinct from kernel/onboarding.py (a WorkflowEngine demo, not a game tutorial).

name: canon
function: Aethryn's LOCKED world canon as machine-checkable data, so generators cannot contradict it (game)
label: canon
reuse: the canon-authority primitive: load_canon validates the world's established facts (the divine strike, Netharion the first artificial god, the Seven Crowns and their functions, the 14 regions + threat bands) at load and fails loud like every seed loader; the CANON_STATUSES ladder (CANON_LOCKED > CANON_WORKING > AUTHORED_LOCAL > GENERATED_LOCAL > RUMOR) is the provenance stamp every future generator writes, and check_canon confirms the shipped world still corresponds to canon (drift caught, never hidden)
notes: The prompt's first law: established canon may NEVER be overwritten by generated content. seeds/aethryn/canon.yaml is the single source; kernel/world/canon.py loads + validates it (exactly 7 CANON_LOCKED crowns, exactly 14 CANON_LOCKED regions with ordered threat bands, facts with id+text, valid statuses) and exposes seven_crowns/regions/locked_region_names/unresolved_questions/is_generated_status. check_canon delegates to a pure _correspondence_violations so the drift guard is unit-testable: today every locked region is a registered waystone zone and every Seven Crown site a registered settlement/dungeon (zero drift). Readable companion: docs/aethryn_lore_bible.md (supersedes the legacy docs/world_bible.md).

name: survey
function: the Surveyor: a read-only developer audit of the Aethryn world map (validate, check-canon, references)
label: survey
reuse: the world-validation primitive: pure checks over the shipped seed (duplicate_ids across files, broken_references to a region canon does not know, and canon.check_canon) whose union is `world validate`; each returns a violation-line list so it is unit-testable and composes; run(argv) is the read-only `world` command family the CLI (tools/world.py) and a Make button call, exit 0 clean / 1 problems / 2 usage
notes: The prompt's developer tools: a `world` command family that validates the world WITHOUT mutating it. This is the read-only half (validate / check-canon / list-regions / list-locations / find-broken-references); the mutating half (generate-area / promote / export / import / inspect / graph / find-unreachable) is planned with the deterministic area generator and is refused honestly (exit 2) rather than faked. Anchors to canon.AETHRYN_DIR so it audits aethryn regardless of the booted seed. tools/world.py is the thin CLI; all logic + tests live in the part.

name: caves
function: the deterministic cave forge: generate one reusable area-family, varied by region, without touching the engine (game)
label: caves
reuse: the local area-generation primitive (the prompt's centerpiece): generate_cave(region, seed) forges a navigable room graph (5-18 rooms, a branch, a loop, a landmark, a hazard, a resource, an optional secret, a micro-story, a return route) that inherits its region's identity from seeds/aethryn/cave_families.yaml; deterministic (sha512-seeded random.Random, same inputs -> identical cave), stamped GENERATED_LOCAL, and self-validating (_validation_report is the generator's own acceptance gate, pinned empty across regions and seeds)
notes: The prompt: expand the world locally WITHOUT inventing global canon. cave_families.yaml is the per-region data (biome, subtypes, entrances, creature/hazard/resource families, landmarks, secrets, naming grammar) the forge composes from, so content stays data. The chain runs on a 4-compass cycle (no axis collides its reverse); branch uses in/out, loop uses up/down, so the graph is always navigable and reciprocal. Generated-lore guardrail: forbidden global canon (gods, pantheon, Netharion's fate) surfaces only as a RUMOR that RAISES a canon.unresolved_question, never asserts it. Sibling of wildlands (MOD-04.070). Next slice wires generate-area/preview/promote/export into the world tool (MOD-04.142).

name: area_store
function: the area bench: preview, save, promote (GENERATED_LOCAL -> AUTHORED_LOCAL), and export generated areas (game)
label: area_store
reuse: the generated-content lifecycle primitive (the prompt's admin loop): generate_and_save -> preview -> promote -> export over a JSON bench (world_areas/, git-ignored, reproducible from seed). promote is the one authority act (a human flips GENERATED_LOCAL to AUTHORED_LOCAL) and refuses anything not GENERATED_LOCAL, so canon or an already-authored area can never be promoted; run(argv) is the mutating half of the `world` CLI, exit 0 ok / 1 refused / 2 usage
notes: Completes the `world` tool family with the mutating commands (generate-area / preview-area / promote / export / list-areas), the read-only half being survey (MOD-04.142). Generated areas are mutable dev state kept APART from static canon in seeds/ (world_areas/ is git-ignored with a tracked README, like reports/ and workspace/). Persistence is plain JSON with sorted keys for a stable round-trip.
